shared_primitives.name: P0 Bridge hardening, shared seams and per-batch test scaffolding
shared_primitives.spec: Prerequisite for every batch; adds no row kinds. (1) A snapshot that Swift rejects falls back to Flutter, never to a blank view. NativeSurfacePlatformView.swift: when NativeSurfaceSnapshot.decode(args) throws on iOS 16+, the factory returns a private RejectedNativeSurface. It registers FlutterMethodChannel('com.omi.native_ui/surface/<viewId>'), answers 'update' with FlutterError(code: 'invalid_native_snapshot'), answers 'invalidate' and 'captureImage' with nil and everything else with FlutterMethodNotImplemented, and clears its handler in deinit. Before iOS 16 UnavailableNativeSurface stays. ios_native_surface.dart: _IosNativeSurfaceState gains bool _rejected. _publish() catches PlatformException(code 'invalid_native_snapshot') at any revision, and MissingPluginException while identical(channel, _channel). It then sets _rejected = true, calls unawaited(_invalidate()) and setState. build() returns _fallback() whenever _rejected is set. This is sticky for the State's lifetime and never flaps. Add a debug-only seam, IosNativeSurface.debugCorruptSnapshotForTest (asserts kDebugMode), that publishes version 2 so a host test can prove this path. (2) ios_native_modal.dart showIosNativeModal: invalid or duplicate rows return null instead of throwing ArgumentError (callers already fall back to their Flutter dialog). PlatformException('invalid_native_presentation') from 'present' also returns null. An unknown action, or a value rejected by NativeRow.accepts, returns NativeModalResult(null, {}) with no mutation instead of throwing. Every native presentation goes through one Dart FIFO (a static future tail), so a call waits for the previous presentation to complete before it invokes 'present'. (3) omi_dialogs.dart showOmiConfirmMenu takes the native shortcut only when iosSwiftUiEnabled && Platform.isIOS. Android built with the flag keeps the anchored Flutter menu. (4) NativeSurfaceView.swift: kind 'label' renders row.symbol as a leading SF Symbol through Label(title:icon:), red when destructive; implement this in the label case, not in label() shared by other kinds. In kind 'task', the title Button sends 'open' only when row.options contains 'open'; otherwise the title is static text. (5) IosNativeSurface gains String? loadingLabel; the snapshot sends loadingLabel ?? l10n.loading. (6) New lib/mobile/native_ui/native_asset_image.dart with Future<String?> nativeAssetImageUri(String asset). It accepts only paths under assets/images/ made of letters, digits, '_', '-' and '/', ending in .png, .jpg, .jpeg or .webp, with no '..'. It loads the rootBundle bytes once per process (one memoized Future per path), writes them atomically to <getTemporaryDirectory()>/omi_native_assets/<sha1(asset)>.<ext> and returns Uri.file(path).toString(), which must pass nativeImageUri. It returns null on any failure. This is static bundled artwork only, never user data, so it needs no session cleanup. Device batches pass the URI to the existing imageUri (72x64 thumbnail) and to image rows. (7) ios_native_settings.dart _settingsSymbols gains FontAwesome mappings for Device Settings rows: handPointer hand.tap, lightbulb lightbulb, download arrow.down.circle, rotateLeft arrow.counterclockwise, sdCard sdcard, stethoscope stethoscope, linkSlash link, ban nosign, graduationCap graduationcap, camera camera, gears gearshape.2, hashtag number, industry building.2, fingerprint touchid, barcode barcode. Verify each name exists in iOS 16 SF Symbols. (8) Cross-batch seam in lib/widgets/components/memory_review_card.dart: Future<void> showMemoryReviewSheet(BuildContext context, {required List<MemoryReviewItem> items, required MemoryReviewSource source, String? impressionKey, String? title}). For now it is implemented as showOmiSheet(builder: SingleChildScrollView(child: MemoryReviewCard(...))), which matches today's recap sheet. After P0 the file belongs to chat-structured-messages, which adds a nativeBuilder; maps-recap only calls the function, and its signature is frozen. (9) Host-test scaffolding: move checkNativeHost, nativeViewId, display/UIKit screenshot capture and the row lookup out of integration_test/native_ui_host_test.dart into the library integration_test/support/native_host_harness.dart. It exports: typedef NativeHostCheck = Future<void> Function(WidgetTester, String); void runNativeHostSuite(void Function(NativeHostCheck checkNativeHost) register), which does binding init and keeps the NATIVE_UI_SCREENSHOT_PORT behaviour; int? nativeViewId(WidgetTester, Finder); NativeRow nativeProjectedRow(WidgetTester, String id), which searches toolbar, sections, bottomBar and chat/reader actions of every mounted IosNativeSurface (last match wins); and Widget nativeHostApp(Widget home, {List<SingleChildWidget> providers, Brightness brightness}), which wraps defaultAuditProviders, l10n and theme. native_ui_host_test.dart keeps every existing case and just calls runNativeHostSuite. Each batch adds its own standalone target, integration_test/native_<batch>_host_test.dart, and never edits native_ui_host_test.dart.
shared_primitives.tests: Dart: native_surface_rejection_test.dart uses a mocked surface channel. An 'update' answered with invalid_native_snapshot, and one that throws MissingPluginException on the current channel, must each render the fallback, stay there after later rebuilds and leave the channel invalidated. A stale channel's MissingPluginException is ignored. native_modal_queue_test.dart: two concurrent showIosNativeModal calls hit 'present' strictly in sequence. A person name longer than its maximumLength returns null instead of throwing. A forged action or value returns NativeModalResult(null, {}). showOmiConfirmMenu keeps the anchored menu when not on iOS. native_asset_image_test.dart: traversal, absolute, uppercase-extension, unknown-extension and missing assets return null; the same asset returns the same URI and is written once. native_surface_projection_test.dart: loadingLabel reaches the snapshot. Swift (Preview): new fixture rows plus testLabelRowRendersSymbol and testTaskTitleWithoutOpenOptionSendsNothing. Host: native_ui_host_test.dart passes unchanged through runNativeHostSuite, and a debugCorruptSnapshotForTest case proves the complete Flutter fallback renders (not a blank UIView) with no uncaught PlatformException.

shared_primitives.name: P1 Native presentation lifecycle: outcome reasons, programmatic dismissal, blocking activity
shared_primitives.spec: Extends the config-channel presenter. There is still exactly one active presentation, guaranteed by the P0 FIFO. Dart (ios_native_modal.dart): NativeModalResult gains final String reason, one of 'action', 'cancel' (explicit cancelId), 'dismissed' (swipe or scrim), 'programmatic', 'invalidated' (account-session change) or 'unmounted'. action stays null for every non-'action' reason, so existing callers are unaffected. A nil response from an older host maps to 'cancel'. showIosNativeModal gains Future<void>? dismissSignal: if it completes before a result, Dart invokes 'dismissPresentation'(id) and returns NativeModalResult(null, {}, reason: 'programmatic'). A native result that arrives after the signal is discarded, and a late signal is ignored. New Future<NativeActivity?> showIosNativeActivity(BuildContext context, {required String label}), label 1..200 chars. It returns null when unsupported, in which case the caller keeps its Flutter spinner dialog. Otherwise it returns a handle whose Future<void> dismiss() is idempotent. The handle also dismisses automatically on session change and when the caller context unmounts. Activities share the FIFO, so an alert requested during an activity waits for it. Swift (NativeModalPresenter.swift, AppDelegate.swift config handler): completion always returns {action: String?, values: {...}, reason: String}. The cancelId toolbar row gives 'cancel', presentationControllerDidDismiss gives 'dismissed' and dismiss(id:) gives 'programmatic'. New config method 'presentActivity' with {requestId, label, appearance, locale, direction}. It presents a UIHostingController(rootView: NativeActivityView) with modalPresentationStyle .overFullScreen, modalTransitionStyle .crossDissolve and isModalInPresentation true. The view has a dimmed background (black at 25%) and a centered card with ProgressView(label), using glassEffect on iOS 26+ and regularMaterial earlier. It adds accessibilityAddTraits(.isModal) and posts a UIAccessibility announcement of the label. It occupies the same active slot and finishes only through dismissPresentation (reason 'programmatic') or session invalidation. Validation: requestId is an Int >= 0; label is non-empty and at most 200 chars; appearance is system, light or dark; direction is ltr or rtl. The presenter rejects the request while another presentation is active.
shared_primitives.tests: Dart, native_presentation_test.dart with a mocked config channel: map every reason (action, cancel, dismissed, programmatic, invalidated, unmounted). A dismissSignal that fires before the result returns 'programmatic' and calls 'dismissPresentation' once; a result that arrives first wins and the late signal is ignored. A nil legacy response maps to cancel. The activity handle's dismiss is idempotent; a session-generation event dismisses it; unsupported returns null; an alert requested during an activity waits for it. Swift Preview: an 'activity' fixture shows the HUD, blocks taps to the content beneath and is dismissed programmatically. Fixtures for modal cancel and swipe report 'cancel' and 'dismissed'. The large-text activity label stays visible.

shared_primitives.name: P2 NativeToast: native transient feedback behind OmiFeedback and AppSnackbar
shared_primitives.spec: Dart: new lib/mobile/native_ui/ios_native_feedback.dart with enum NativeToastKind {confirm, info, error, undo, progress} and enum NativeToastOutcome {action, closed, swiped, timeout, replaced, invalidated}. class NativeToastRequest has these fields: int requestId, strictly increasing per process; kind; message, 1..1000 graphemes with no U+0000; String? actionLabel, 1..40 graphemes, required for undo, allowed for error only when an onAction exists, null otherwise; String? closeLabel, error only; int durationMs, which must equal OmiFeedbackTiming for the kind (1500, 4000, 8000, 5000, 60000); String symbol, from an allowlist (checkmark.circle.fill, info.circle, exclamationmark.circle.fill, trash, person, tv, progress); double bottomClearance, finite and in 0..240; appearance (system, light or dark), locale and direction (ltr or rtl). It exposes Map projection and bool valid. Future<NativeToastOutcome?> showIosNativeToast(NativeToastRequest) invokes config 'toast' and completes when the toast ends. It returns null on MissingPluginException, an invalid request or FlutterError('invalid_native_toast'). Future<void> dismissIosNativeToast() invokes 'dismissToast'. NativeFeedbackHost.active is a synchronous bool that becomes true only after supportsIosSwiftUi() resolves true; set it inside supportsIosSwiftUi in ios_native_home.dart, which already requires iosSwiftUiEnabled && Platform.isIOS. The first toast subscribes to AuthService.sessionGenerationEvents and dismisses on any change. omi_feedback.dart: when NativeFeedbackHost.active, _show maps kind and icon (Icons.person* to person, Icons.tv* to tv, delete glyphs to trash, otherwise the kind default) and clearance (the existing _extraBottom(context)) into a request and fires it. If it gets null back, it shows today's SnackBar unchanged. undo() resolves true only for outcome action, after onUndo has run, and false for every other outcome, matching SnackBarClosedReason != action. error with onAction runs onAction on action. hide() also calls dismissIosNativeToast. A newer request completes the previous one with replaced. AppSnackbar needs no change because it delegates to OmiFeedback. ios_native_main_navigation.dart: while the native shell is mounted, it sets OmiFeedback.bottomClearance to 64 (the tab-bar reserve), plus the native Home footer height on the Home tab (a constant matched to NativeHomeView). It restores the previous closure on dispose, and the classic shell is untouched. Swift: NativeToastRequest is Decodable with validate() in NativeSurfaceContract.swift (Foundation only, so the Ruby contract test compiles it). New NativeToastPresenter.swift, @MainActor and owned by AppDelegate next to NativeModalPresenter, handles config methods 'toast' and 'dismissToast'. It keeps one PassthroughWindow per active UIWindowScene at windowLevel .normal + 1, above Flutter, platform views and presented sheets. hitTest returns nil outside the toast frame, and the window is hidden and released when idle. Its root is a UIHostingController(NativeToastView): a capsule with Image(systemName:) (or ProgressView for progress), Text(message).lineLimit(4), an optional accent action Button and an optional close Button(xmark) with accessibilityLabel(closeLabel). It uses glassEffect(.regular.interactive(), in: .capsule) on iOS 26+ and a regularMaterial capsule earlier. Bottom offset = max(keyboard overlap from UIKeyboard notifications, bottomClearance) + safeAreaInsets.bottom + 12. Outcomes: drag down past 24pt gives swiped, Task.sleep(duration) gives timeout, the action button gives action, the close button gives closed, a new request makes the previous one replaced, and dismissToast gives invalidated. On appear it posts a UIAccessibility announcement. With Reduce Motion it uses an opacity transition only. overrideUserInterfaceStyle and layoutDirection follow the request. Nothing is persisted or logged. Add NativeToastPresenter.swift to both Runner targets and the Preview project.
shared_primitives.tests: Dart, native_toast_test.dart: request validation covers kind/duration mismatch, an action on confirm, a missing undo label, close on undo, non-finite clearance and an over-long message. Outcome mapping: undo returns true only for action, and onUndo runs before resolution. replaced, timeout, swiped and invalidated all return false. error onAction runs exactly once. With NativeFeedbackHost.active false (flag off or Android), the config channel is never touched and the SnackBar path is byte-identical (existing ui_feedback tests stay green). A null result falls back to the SnackBar. A session-generation event dismisses. Swift contract test: rejects unknown kind, duration mismatch, action on confirm/info/progress, close on undo, non-finite or out-of-range clearance, and non-increasing requestId. Preview: a toast above a presented pageSheet is hittable; taps outside the toast reach the content below; VoiceOver announcement; RTL and accessibility text sizes; keyboard avoidance; swipe-down outcome.

shared_primitives.name: P3 One-time secret reveal: secret row kind, sensitive surface, showIosNativeSecretSheet
shared_primitives.spec: Dart (ios_native_surface.dart): new NativeRow kind 'secret'. value is the credential String, 1..4096 chars, every char in 0x21..0x7E (printable ASCII, no whitespace or newline). options must be exactly {'copy': <localized label>}, and accepts(input) is true only for input == 'copy'. imageUri, points, blocks, level, maximumValue, keyboard, maximumLength, indent, swipe ids and graph must all be null or empty. IosNativeSurface gains bool sensitive (snapshot key 'sensitive'). build() falls back when a secret row appears in toolbar, bottomBar, chat, reader or navigation; when there is more than one secret row; when a secret row is present with sensitive false; or when sensitive is combined with publicSurface, chat, reader, navigation, selection or a fill graph. When sensitive, NativeSurfaceController.captureImage returns null without calling the host. showIosNativeModal returns null when any row is 'secret', because the presenter echoes values back. New lib/mobile/native_ui/ios_native_secret.dart: bool nativeSecretValid(String) and Future<void> showIosNativeSecretSheet(BuildContext context, {required String title, String? message, String? warning, required String secretLabel, required String secret, required String copyLabel, required String doneLabel, required VoidCallback onCopy, required Future<void> Function() showClassic}). It calls showClassic when the flag is off, the platform is not iOS, supportsIosSwiftUi() is false or the secret is invalid. Otherwise it captures AuthService.captureSessionSnapshot() and opens showOmiSheet(isDismissible: false, enableDrag: false, nativeBuilder: ...). That page is PopScope(canPop: false) wrapping IosNativeSurface(sensitive: true, title, toolbar [NativeRow('secret_done', doneLabel, symbol 'checkmark')], sections [label message, label warning with symbol exclamationmark.triangle, NativeRow('secret_value', secretLabel, kind 'secret', value: secret, options {'copy': copyLabel}, action: (_) => onCopy())]). Its fallback is a minimal Flutter body (monospace SelectableText of the secret, Copy and Done, using only the passed labels), so the P0 rejection path never loses the one-time key. Done or a session-generation change pops the route. The secret is never logged, never part of a row id and never cached. Swift: the decoder allowlists 'secret' and the top-level sensitive: Bool?; validation mirrors Dart (unicodeScalars all in 0x21...0x7E with count 1...4096, options exactly [copy], sections only, at most one per snapshot, requires sensitive == true). rowView case 'secret': VStack(alignment: .leading) with Text(row.title) in caption semibold secondary; Text(verbatim: value) in .body.monospaced() with .textSelection(.enabled), .privacySensitive() and vertical fixedSize; the subtitle in footnote secondary; and Button { send(row.id, 'copy') } label: Label(copy title, systemImage: 'doc.on.doc') with .buttonStyle(.bordered). The row is exempt from the label-kind disabled rule, and its accessibilityIdentifier is row.id only. When snapshot.sensitive is set, the view observes UIApplication.willResignActiveNotification and didBecomeActiveNotification. While inactive it shows content as .redacted(reason: .privacy) under an ultraThinMaterial overlay, so the app-switcher snapshot hides the key. NativeSurfacePlatformView 'captureImage' returns nil when snapshot.sensitive. withoutContent() resets sensitive to false. NativeModalPresenter.present throws .invalid when any row is 'secret'.
shared_primitives.tests: Dart, native_secret_test.dart: a secret that is empty, 4097 chars, contains whitespace or a newline, or contains non-ASCII is invalid. accepts allows only 'copy'. A secret with sensitive false, in the toolbar, doubled, or combined with chat or selection falls back. A modal containing a secret returns null. The routine snapshot JSON contains the secret only inside the secret row value. captureImage returns null on a sensitive surface. showIosNativeSecretSheet calls showClassic when unsupported or invalid, never presents after a session change, and pops on Done. Swift contract: accepts a valid secret in a sensitive snapshot; rejects a non-sensitive snapshot, newline, 4097 chars, a non-copy option, a secret in the toolbar, and two secret rows. Preview fixture 'secret': monospaced value; copy sends exactly 'copy' (never the value); posting willResignActive redacts and didBecomeActive restores; session invalidation clears the value.

shared_primitives.name: P4 List interactions: multi-selection with bottom bar, section reorder, indent, collapsible sections, swipe actions
shared_primitives.spec: Dart (ios_native_surface.dart): (a) class NativeSelection {const NativeSelection({required Set<String> selected, required Set<String> selectable, required NativeAction action}); projection {'selected': sorted list, 'selectable': sorted list}; bool validFor(Iterable<NativeSection>) is true when selectable has at most 10000 ids, every selectable id is a section row id and every selected id is selectable}. IosNativeSurface gains NativeSelection? selection and List<NativeRow> bottomBar (snapshot keys 'selection' and 'bottomBar'). dispatchNativeAction gains optional named NativeSelection? selection and Iterable<NativeSection> sections. id '_selection' with a List value whose elements are unique Strings, at most 10000, all selectable, calls selection.action(List<String>); owners treat it as the desired set and diff idempotently. bottomBar rows dispatch like toolbar rows. (b) bottomBar: at most 6 rows of kinds label (at most one), button and menu. Ids must be unique across toolbar, sections, bottomBar and chat/reader actions. Not allowed with chat, reader, navigation or a fill graph. (c) NativeSection gains NativeAction? reorder (projection 'reorderable': reorder != null) and bool collapsible (projection 'collapsible', requires a non-empty title). A reorderable section may contain only rows of kind task, navigation, label, toggle or menu. Command '_reorder:<sectionId>' takes a List value that must be an exact permutation of that section's current row ids (same length, unique, set-equal) and calls section.reorder(List<String>); anything else throws PlatformException('invalid_native_action'). Selection and reorderable sections are mutually exclusive. (d) NativeRow gains int? indent (0..3; kinds task, navigation, label, toggle, menu) and List<String> swipeLeading and swipeTrailing. Each swipe id must be in options.keys, with at most 3 per edge and no id on both edges; kinds task, navigation, menu. Dispatch is unchanged (value = option id), so every swipe action is also reachable from the context menu. (e) IosNativeSurface fills snapshot keys 'expandLabel' (l10n.expand) and 'collapseLabel' (l10n.collapseAction), the way it fills retry and loadingLabel. Swift (NativeSurfaceContract.swift, NativeSurfaceView.swift, and a new NativeListInteractions.swift added to both Runner targets and the Preview project): decode Selection {selected, selectable: [String]}; bottomBar: [NativeSurfaceRow]?, included in allRows; Section.reorderable and .collapsible: Bool?; Row.indent: Int?; Row.swipeLeading and .swipeTrailing: [String]?; expandLabel and collapseLabel: String?. Validation mirrors Dart exactly. replacingValue carries the new fields and withoutContent clears them. NativeModalPresenter rejects any of them. NativeSurfaceState gains optimisticSelection: Set<String>? and optimisticOrders: [String: [String]]. They apply immediately on user change and are dropped when a newer snapshot arrives while the command is not pending, or on failure. '_selection' and '_reorder:*' count as edits (latest value wins), and non-edit actions such as bottom-bar Delete wait for them, the way Save waits for text edits. Rendering applies in list mode only, never in reader or chat. Selection: List(selection: Binding(get: optimistic ?? selected, set: send the new set intersected with selectable, sorted, as '_selection')) with .environment(.editMode, .constant(.active)). Selectable rows render as static label(row) with no buttons, context menus or swipes. Other rows keep their control with .selectionDisabled(true) on iOS 17+; on iOS 16 they are disabled during selection and the setter filters them out. Reorderable sections: edit mode active, rows static, ForEach.onMove builds the full id permutation, applies it optimistically and sends '_reorder:<id>'; the system reorder controls provide VoiceOver drag. Collapsible: the header is a Button with chevron.down/chevron.up and the title, .isHeader trait and an accessibilityHint of expandLabel or collapseLabel. The collapsed set is view @State, cleared on invalidate, and rows are omitted while collapsed. Indent: .padding(.leading, indent * 20) with a 1.5pt quaternary Capsule rule when indent > 0. Swipes: .swipeActions(edge:, allowsFullSwipe: true) with buttons titled from options, role .destructive for 'delete', and systemImage from an allowlist (delete trash, complete checkmark.circle, reopen arrow.uturn.backward.circle, pin pin, unpin pin.slash, star star, unstar star.slash, review_right hand.thumbsup, review_wrong hand.thumbsdown, otherwise none). Swipes are suppressed while selecting or reordering. bottomBar: .safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom) { NativeGlassControls { ViewThatFits(in: .horizontal) { HStack(label, Spacer, buttons); VStack(label, buttons) } }.padding(12).background(.bar) }, with buttons from rowView(compact: true).modifier(NativeGlassButtonStyle()), destructive role, and disabled when !enabled or pending. Inside the native shell it sits above the separate tab-bar surface.
shared_primitives.tests: Dart, native_list_interactions_test.dart: validFor (selectable not a subset of rows, selected not a subset of selectable, more than 10000). '_selection' rejects non-list values, non-strings, duplicates and unknown ids, and passes a List<String> through. bottomBar limits on kinds, count, labels and id uniqueness, plus the chat/reader/fill-graph conflicts. '_reorder' rejects duplicates, missing, extra, foreign and stale ids and accepts an exact permutation. Selection plus reorder falls back. indent bounds and kinds. Swipe ids must be a subset of options, edges disjoint, at most 3 per edge. collapsible requires a title. Swift contract: accept and reject for each new field. Preview fixtures: 'selection' (edit-mode circles; tap toggles optimistically; the sorted set is sent; a non-selectable Show more row stays usable on iOS 17; bottom-bar Delete waits for the pending selection; large text keeps the bottom bar reachable), 'reorder' (drag sends the full permutation; a failure reverts to the snapshot order), 'collapsible' (rows hidden, VoiceOver hint), 'swipe' (sends the option id; no swipe while selecting), 'indent' (rule visible, row height unchanged).

shared_primitives.name: P5 Chat rendering extensions: rich message_ai bodies with link whitelist, bar/line categorical charts
shared_primitives.spec: Dart: NativeRow.valid allows blocks on kinds rich_text and message_ai (same RichBlock rules), forbids plainText together with blocks, and caps message_ai at 2,000 blocks; rich_text keeps its current limits. message_ai accepts null or an options key. Options are the link whitelist from nativeRichTextLinks of the same Markdown, and the Dart owner opens them through the existing launchUrl owner. New field String? chartStyle, 'line' or 'bar' (projection 'chartStyle'), valid only on kind chart. When set, points must have x = 0..n-1 in index order, finite y, label at most 64 chars, and 1 <= n <= 10,000. Swift: decoding mirrors this (blocks only on rich_text or message_ai; chartStyle only on chart with those two values). NativeSurfaceView.message(row): when blocks is non-empty, render NativeRichTextView(row:state:query: '') inside the bubble layout, keeping the frames preference used for visibility. For message_ai, its OpenURLAction discards any URL that is not an option id, even when options is empty (never .systemAction). Rows without blocks keep today's Text path and trailing-button behaviour. Rows with blocks show the trailing button only when row.symbol is set, so a link whitelist never adds a stray button. case chart: with chartStyle nil, the existing LineMark rendering is unchanged (Usage keeps it). With chartStyle set, render from 1 point, height 200. 'bar' draws BarMark(x: .value(subtitle, point.x), y: .value(title, point.y)). 'line' draws LineMark plus PointMark with .interpolationMethod(.catmullRom). .chartXAxis uses AxisMarks over the thinned x values (first, last and every ceil(n/6)th index) with AxisValueLabel showing that point's label. Add .accessibilityLabel(title).
shared_primitives.tests: Dart, native_chat_rendering_test.dart: message_ai with valid blocks is valid. plainText plus blocks is invalid, and 2,001 blocks are invalid. A link is accepted only when it is an options key. chartStyle is valid only on chart with line or bar. Non-index x, NaN y and a 65-char label are rejected. The Usage chart without chartStyle is unchanged. Swift contract: the same accept/reject matrix. Preview fixtures: 'chat-rich' renders a table, code, list and quote in an AI bubble; a non-whitelisted link is discarded and a whitelisted one sends its id; an AI row with blocks and no symbol shows no trailing button. 'chart-bar' and 'chart-line' cover long labels, a single point and large text.

shared_primitives.name: P6 Knowledge-graph row kind (card and fill stage), native camera, row-scoped capture
shared_primitives.spec: Dart: new lib/mobile/native_ui/native_graph.dart, which must not import ios_native_surface.dart. It defines NativeGraphNode(id, label, type, x, y, z, fixed), NativeGraphEdge(source, target, label), NativeGraph({nodes, edges, highlighted = const {}, zoom = 1.0, interactive = true, layout = 'fill', double? height, required String accent}) and NativeGraph.placeholder({layout = 'fill', height, required accent}). Projection: {nodes: [{id, label, type, x, y, z, fixed}], edges: [{source, target, label}], highlighted: sorted, zoom, interactive, layout, height, placeholder, accent}, plus nodeIds and valid. NativeRow gains NativeGraph? graph (projection 'graph'), and kind 'graph' holds exactly when graph != null. When interactive, value is '' or a node id, and accepts takes a String that is '' or a current node id; otherwise value is null and accepts takes only null. Validation is identical in Swift. A placeholder has no nodes or edges and interactive false. Otherwise: 1..1024 nodes and at most 4096 edges; node id 1..256 chars and unique; label at most 256 chars; type in {user, person, place, organization, thing, concept}; x, y and z finite with |v| <= 1e6; at most one fixed node, and it must be type user at (0,0,0). Each edge has source != target, both endpoints present, label at most 128 chars, and a unique (source, target, label). highlighted is a subset of the nodes, at most 5 entries, and empty when value is ''. zoom is finite in [0.05, 5]. layout is fill or card. A card has height in [100, 600] and interactive false; a fill graph has height null. At most one fill graph per snapshot. When a fill graph is present, the snapshot has no search, chat, reader, navigation, selection, bottomBar or refresh, and every other section row is label or button; toolbar rows are unrestricted. accent is # followed by 6 hex digits. NativeSurfaceController.captureImage({String? target}): the target must be the id of a current, valid, non-placeholder graph row, otherwise the result is null. It invokes 'captureImage' with {'target': id} under the same session, mounted, channel and 16 MB checks as today. Swift: NativeSurfaceContract.swift decodes and validates Graph, Node and Edge. New NativeGraphView.swift goes in both Runner targets and the Preview project. NativeGraphCanvas is a SwiftUI Canvas that reproduces the Flutter GraphPainter3D math: rotate Y then X; cameraZ 1500; perspective = 1500/(1500 - z) * zoom; alpha = clamp(1 + z/2500); back-to-front order. Nodes get a radial gradient fill with halo rings at 1.8r and 2.5r; edge stroke is 0.8 * scale. Node labels draw when scale > 0.7 && alpha > 0.5 && r > 4, and edge labels when the average scale > 0.6. When a selection exists, non-highlighted elements dim to 15%. Labels get backgrounds in the light scheme. Fixed palette: person #18FFFF, place #00FF9D, organization #FFAB40, thing #FFFF00, concept #448AFF, user = accent. The camera (rotX, rotY, panX, panY, zoom) lives only in NativeSurfaceState.graphCameras[row.id]; it resets when the sorted node-id set changes and is never sent to Dart. graphSizes keeps the last rendered size. Gestures go through a UIViewRepresentable overlay. A one-finger pan rotates at 0.005 rad/pt, a two-finger pan pans, and a pinch zooms within 0.05..5. A tap hit-tests the nearest projected node within max(radius * 1.5, 20)pt, capped at 30pt, and sends (row.id, nodeId), or '' for the background. No other gesture sends anything. Card layout: a fixed-height List row; the whole card is a Button that sends nil. Fill layout: NativeSurfaceView.content switches to a non-scrolling stage. excluded_with_reason: PaymentWebViewPage (subscription checkout and customer portal): Dart's NavigationDelegate intercepts the /v1/payments/success and /cancel URLs to resolve the plan flow. SFSafariViewController cannot intercept navigations, and a SwiftUI web primitive would move checkout ownership. The content is already a native WKWebView, and the docs say checkout stays with its existing owner.

OmiWebPage (Referral program, affiliate.omi.me) and AppHomeWebPage (an app's web home): the content is already a native WKWebView running arbitrary JavaScript. Native chrome would need a web primitive inside the SwiftUI renderer, which is a new browser surface with cookie and session ownership. An SFSafariViewController hand-off changes the cookie/login store and history-back behaviour, so it needs product sign-off.

DeviceSelectionPage (signed-out welcome): its presentation is a looping branded video (assets/images/onboarding.mp4) behind two lines of copy and one Get Started button that leads into the already-native onboarding. Reproducing it needs a looping-video primitive that no other screen needs, and dropping the video is a brand decision for design. Keep it in Flutter and revisit only if a video or hero primitive is justified elsewhere.

QuickLook preview of chat composer attachments: Flutter has no such viewer, so this would be a new feature, not a migration. It adds system-side parsing of untrusted Office/PDF files and a share/export path, and needs product sign-off.

Full viewers for historical non-image chat attachments and full-resolution historical chat images: the backend keeps no downloadable copy (non-image files go to OpenAI by file id; images keep only a 128px thumbnail), and Flutter has no viewer either. A viewer would need a new backend endpoint and download owner, which is outside presentation migration.

Memories multi-select and global-search result multi-select: neither exists in Flutter (MemoriesProvider has no selection API and global_search.dart has none). Adding them would be new product features; the ledger wording is corrected instead.

Training-data opt-in in the plans sheet: it is dormant behind const _showTrainingDataOptIn = false and intentionally forces the classic renderer. Keep it classic until the program is re-enabled so its consent renderer is not lost.
CustomErrorWidget (the main.dart render-failure screen, including its 'error copied' SnackBar): the crash/render fallback path must never depend on the native bridge.
Whisper confirmModelDownload dialog: only reachable on Android (iOS on-device transcription uses native speech), so there is no iOS presentation to migrate.

Transcription JSON request/schema editor content above 262,144 UTF-16 units: by documented design it stays on the complete Flutter editor, reached automatically when a stored or imported configuration exceeds the cap; native import reads the clipboard uncapped in Dart. A chunked native document editor (UITextView with a delta and read protocol) is not justified for this edge case.

Decorative, animation-only visuals with no functional content: device tutorial demo animations and glow, the scanning ripple, Wrapped story-style paging, card animations and pie painter, shimmer placeholders, the Stripe pulse ring, and brand SVG logos (Stripe, Omi hero pair). No illustration, story or video primitive is added. The native screens present the same data and actions with SF Symbols, bundled artwork thumbnails, progress rows and lists, and the animated versions remain in each screen's classic fallback.

External and system UIs that are already native and owned elsewhere: Stripe onboarding in the external browser, Apple/Google Maps hand-off, the Intercom messenger, the sms: composer, the system share sheet, the StoreKit review sheet and the Shortcuts app.

Interactive MapKit maps for the conversation map and recap journey: MapKit would fetch tiles for users' conversation locations from Apple, bypassing the backend's single-provider static-map seam, which is a privacy and provider change. Maps stay as Dart-fetched static images, with an explicit-tap MapsUtil hand-off.
NativeHomeView recap-card map thumbnails: purely decorative, they would require a NativeHomeContract change, and the same data is reachable through the recap detail journey sheet.
